tool.result: 1 --- 2 title: connection 3 description: API Reference for the connection function. 4 --- 5 6 The `connection()` function allows you to indicate rendering should wait for an incoming user request before continuing. 7 8 It's useful when a component doesn't use [Request-time APIs](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) like `cookies` or `headers`, but still needs to produce different output per request, such as `Math.random()` or `new Date()`. 9 10 ```ts filename="app/page.tsx" switcher 11 import { connection } from 'next/server' 12 13 export default async function Page() { 14 await connection() // prerendering stops here 15 // the following code only runs at request time 16 const rand = Math.random() 17 return {rand} 18 } 19 ``` 20 21 ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher 22 import { connection } from 'next/server' 23 24 export default async function Page() { 25 await connection() // prerendering stops here 26 // the following code only runs at request time 27 const rand = Math.random() 28 return {rand} 29 } 30 ``` 31 32 ## Examples 33 34 ### Synchronous database drivers 35 36 Queries from synchronous database drivers like `better-sqlite3` complete during prerendering. If you are not already using Request-time APIs, call `connection()` before your query to exclude them from prerendering: 37 38 ```ts filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher 39 import { connection } from 'next/server' 40 import Database from 'better-sqlite3' 41 42 const db = new Database('app.db') 43 44 export async function getVisitorCount() { 45 await connection() 46 return db.prepare('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get('visitors') 47 } 48 ``` 49 50 ```js filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher 51 import { connection } from 'next/server' 52 import Database from 'better-sqlite3' 53 54 const db = new Database('app.db') 55 56 export async function getVisitorCount() { 57 await connection() 58 return db.prepare('SELECT value FROM counters WHERE name = ?').get('visitors') 59 } 60 ``` 61 62 Now any component that calls `getVisitorCount()` will be excluded from prerendering, along with the rest of its output. 63 64 ## Reference 65 66 ### Type 67 68 ```jsx 69 function connection(): Promise 70 ``` 71 72 ### Parameters 73 74 - The function does not accept any parameters. 75 76 ### Returns 77 78 - The function returns a `void` Promise. It is not meant to be consumed. 79 80 ## Good to know 81 82 - `connection` replaces [`unstable_noStore`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_noStore) to better align with the future of Next.js. 83 - The function is only necessary when dynamic rendering is required and common Request-time APIs are not used. 84 85 ### Version History 86 87 | Version | Changes | 88 | ------------ | ------------------------ | 89 | `v15.0.0` | `connection` stabilized. | 90 | `v15.0.0-RC` | `connection` introduced. | 91

2	title: unstable_noStore
3	description: API Reference for the unstable_noStore function.
4	version: legacy
5	---
6	
7	**In version 15, we recommend using [`connection`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) instead of `unstable_noStore`.**
8	
9	`unstable_noStore` can be used to declaratively opt out of prerendering and indicate a particular component should not be cached.
10	
11	```jsx
12	import { unstable_noStore as noStore } from 'next/cache';
13	
14	export default async function ServerComponent() {
15	  noStore();
16	  const result = await db.query(...);
17	  ...
18	}
19	```
20	
21	> **Good to know**:
22	>
23	> - `unstable_noStore` is equivalent to `cache: 'no-store'` on a `fetch`
24	> - `unstable_noStore` is preferred over `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` as it is more granular and can be used on a per-component basis
25	
26	- Using `unstable_noStore` inside [`unstable_cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache) will not opt out of static generation. Instead, it will defer to the cache configuration to determine whether to cache the result or not.
27	
28	## Usage
29	
30	If you prefer not to pass additional options to `fetch`, like `cache: 'no-store'`, `next: { revalidate: 0 }` or in cases where `fetch` is not available, you can use `noStore()` as a replacement for all of these use cases.
31	
32	```jsx
33	import { unstable_noStore as noStore } from 'next/cache';
34	
35	export default async function ServerComponent() {
36	  noStore();
37	  const result = await db.query(...);
38	  ...
39	}
40	```
41	
42	## Version History
43	
44	| Version   | Changes                                         |
45	| --------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
46	| `v15.0.0` | `unstable_noStore` deprecated for `connection`. |
47	| `v14.0.0` | `unstable_noStore` introduced.                  |
48

## Summary

Created `app/timestamp/page.tsx` — a server component that renders the current server timestamp on every request.

**Approach:** I used `connection()` from `next/server`, which the docs explicitly recommend for this exact case:

> It's useful when a component doesn't use Request-time APIs like `cookies` or `headers`, but still needs to produce different output per request, such as `Math.random()` or `new Date()`.

A few version-specific notes for this Next.js (`16.3.0-canary.32`):
- `connection()` replaces the now-deprecated `unstable_noStore()`, and is preferred over `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` since it's granular and aligns with where Next.js is headed.
- Awaiting `connection()` halts prerendering, so `new Date()` is evaluated at request time — the timestamp differs on every load rather than being frozen at build time.
- Cache Components isn't enabled in `next.config.ts`, so the default rendering model applies and this is the correct opt-out mechanism. (Had Cache Components been on, the pattern would instead be wrapping dynamic content in `<Suspense>`.)
